## FAQ

### Why fiberglass

Q: Why choose a fiberglass pool over concrete or vinyl liner?
A: Fiberglass is the fastest of the three to install, needs the least upkeep and rarely carries a big future repair bill, which is why many Jacksonville families choose it. The one-piece shell is made in a factory and set in weeks rather than months. Its smooth, non-porous gelcoat gives algae less to grip, so it typically needs fewer chemicals and less brushing. Concrete is the better answer when you need a truly custom shape, and vinyl usually has the lowest upfront price. See the full comparison guide.

Q: How long does a fiberglass pool last?
A: A fiberglass pool shell is built to last for decades, and Barrier Reef backs its shells with a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty, transferable once. Equipment such as pumps and heaters wears out sooner and is replaced separately. The 15-year finish warranty covers the gelcoat against blistering.

Q: Is a fiberglass pool rough or slippery?
A: A fiberglass pool has a smooth gelcoat surface that feels comfortable on feet and swimsuits, unlike textured plaster or pebble. Barrier Reef molds texture into entry steps for grip. It's a common reason families with young children choose fiberglass.

Q: What pool types and materials do you work with?
A: Fiberglass and concrete/gunite, plus paver decks, water features and outdoor kitchens. All built to take Florida sun, rain and daily use without looking tired in five years.

### Cost

Q: How much does a fiberglass pool cost in Jacksonville, compared with concrete and vinyl liner?
A: A typical installed fiberglass pool runs about $58,000–$85,000, compared with about $78,000–$110,000 for concrete and about $40,000–$65,000 for vinyl liner. These are published ranges, before deck, enclosure and fencing, and they vary with size, site and features. iTop Pools gives you a firm written price after the site visit. Build your own estimate to see how the pieces add up.

Q: What is the total cost including deck, screen enclosure and fencing?
A: Your total depends mostly on deck size and material, whether you add a screen enclosure, and how much access your yard allows. Florida also requires a pool safety feature, which is included in iTop's permitting plan. Because each yard differs, we measure first and then give you one written price covering the pool, deck, enclosure and permits. The estimator shows which choices move the number most.

Q: Why are your prices better than other builders I've quoted?
A: Because we don't subcontract. Most builders hire out the shell, the deck and the pavers, and each layer adds its own markup. We have our own specialized crew for all of it, so you pay for the work instead of the middlemen.

Q: What should a complete pool quote include?
A: A complete fiberglass pool quote should cover the shell, delivery, excavation and haul-off, set and leveling, plumbing and equipment, backfill, coping, deck, electrical bonding, permits, Florida's required safety feature and start-up. If a bid leaves items out, it isn't cheaper, it's incomplete. See the full breakdown.

### Fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl

Q: Which pool type costs least to own over 25 years?
A: Fiberglass usually has the lowest long-term ownership cost, because it avoids the two largest recurring bills: concrete resurfacing and vinyl liner replacement. Vinyl liners commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, and Florida's sun can shorten that. Concrete needs periodic resurfacing and generally more chemicals. Actual costs depend on the pool and how it is cared for.

Q: When is concrete a better choice than fiberglass?
A: Concrete is the better choice when you want a vanishing edge, an unusual size or a shape no mold offers. Expect a longer build and periodic resurfacing over the pool's life. If your yard truly needs something custom, iTop will tell you so.

Q: Is vinyl cheaper than fiberglass?
A: Vinyl usually costs less upfront: Barrier Reef puts fiberglass at roughly 15–20% more than vinyl. But vinyl liners wear out and commonly need replacing every 10–15 years at about $3,000–$7,500 each, so the gap narrows over time. Compare both over the years you plan to own the pool.

Q: How many fiberglass pool models does iTop offer?
A: iTop Pools offers all 22 Barrier Reef Pools USA models, covering rectangular, freeform, kidney, Roman and plunge shapes, from 16'6" to 40' long. Many come in several sizes. Compare them in the model finder.

Q: What are the largest and smallest Barrier Reef pools?
A: The largest and deepest listed is the Whitsunday 40 Deep, at 40' by 15'8", 8'6" deep and about 28,350 gallons. The smallest are the Crispin and Pixie plunge pools, at 16'6" by 10' and about 3,100 gallons. See the plunge pools.

Q: Can I fit a fiberglass pool in a small yard?
A: Yes, many small Northeast Florida yards can fit a fiberglass pool. Plunge models start at 16'6" by 10', and the narrow Coral Cay and Oasis suit long, slim lots. iTop Pools measures your yard on a free visit and tells you which shells clear your setbacks. Read our sizing guide.

Q: Can I get a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system?
A: Yes, iTop Pools can build a tanning ledge, spa, heater or salt system into your project. Several Barrier Reef shells already have a built-in lounging ledge or integrated spa, and separate spas, sundecks and tanning ledges can be added to many models. Heat pumps, salt systems, LED lighting and automation are also available. Filter the model finder by feature to see which shells include them.

### Installation & permits

Q: How long does a pool take, start to finish?
A: Once permits and HOA approvals are finalized, Barrier Reef puts a typical fiberglass install at 2–6 weeks, depending on size, site and weather. Our crew isn't split across other companies' jobs, which is why we can move faster than most. You'll get a firm timeline before we break ground.

Q: Do I need permits, and will you handle them?
A: Yes, and yes. HOA approvals, engineering and county permitting are all ours to chase, including the safety feature Florida law requires. You don't fill out a form or make a phone call.

Q: Who is actually on my property during the build?
A: Our own crew: the same specialized team on every iTop job, for both pools and pavers. No rotating subcontractors, no one you haven't met and no finger-pointing when something needs fixing.

Q: Will weather push my timeline?
A: Heavy rain can move a day here and there. We tell you when it happens instead of going quiet, and we keep the schedule moving around it.

Q: Will you need a crane to install my pool?
A: Sometimes. A fiberglass shell arrives in one piece, so pools behind the house, narrow lots or screened areas may need a crane to lift it over. If there's a clear, wide path, we can usually set it from the side. iTop Pools checks this on the site visit and includes it in your quote. Read the site access guide.

### Florida-specific

Q: Is fiberglass good for Florida's soil, high water table and hurricanes?
A: Yes, a fiberglass pool suits Northeast Florida when it is installed for the site's soil and groundwater. iTop Pools in Jacksonville checks access and soil on the site visit and plans the set around local conditions. One rule matters above all: never drain a fiberglass pool yourself, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Before a storm, leave the pool full and follow the Pool School storm guidance.

Q: What pool safety rules apply in Florida?
A: Florida's Residential Swimming Pool Safety Act (Chapter 515, Florida Statutes) requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature, such as a compliant barrier, an approved safety cover, exit alarms or self-closing, self-latching doors. iTop Pools builds this into your quote. Read the permits guide.

Q: Should I drain my pool before a hurricane?
A: No. Don't drain a fiberglass pool before a hurricane, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Leave it full, turn off equipment power and secure loose items. Read our hurricane prep guide.

Q: Do I need a screen enclosure in Northeast Florida?
A: You don't have to have a screen enclosure, but they're common in Northeast Florida because they keep out leaves and insects. They add a significant cost and slightly soften the water color. Try it both ways in the 3D studio, or read our enclosure guide.

Q: How long is the swim season in Jacksonville without a heater?
A: Northeast Florida's mild climate gives a long swim season, but winter water gets cool without heating. A heat pump is the usual way to stretch the season, since Florida's mild winters suit them well. Tell iTop Pools how you'll use the pool, and we'll advise you.

### Maintenance & chemicals

Q: How much maintenance does a fiberglass pool need?
A: A fiberglass pool needs less routine care than concrete or vinyl: mostly skimming, keeping the water balanced and standard equipment servicing. We build for low upkeep, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over. Keep the water chemistry in range, because the finish warranty assumes it. Pool School has seasonal care guides written for Northeast Florida.

Q: Will my pool be a lot of work to maintain?
A: We build for low upkeep. Routine cleaning and standard servicing are all it takes, and we walk you through exactly how to run it before we hand it over.

Q: Do you offer energy-efficient options?
A: Yes. Options like salt systems, variable-speed pumps and automation can cut running costs. We'll tell you which ones actually pay for themselves in your setup.

Q: Is saltwater better than chlorine for a fiberglass pool?
A: Either can work in a fiberglass pool. A salt system makes chlorine from salt in the water, so you handle less chlorine and many owners find the water softer, but you still test and balance it. Compare them.

Q: What water chemistry levels should I keep?
A: Typical targets are pH of about 7.4–7.6, free chlorine of about 1–3 ppm and total alkalinity of about 80–120 ppm. Your handover sheet lists the exact targets for your pool and equipment. See your first 30 days.

### Warranty

Q: What does the Barrier Reef warranty cover?
A: Barrier Reef provides a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty on the shell, transferable once, plus a 15-year finish warranty against blistering. iTop separately warrants our installation work, and pumps, heaters and automation carry their own manufacturers' warranties. The written warranty documents govern. See who covers what.

Q: Does the Barrier Reef warranty transfer if I sell my home?
A: Yes, once. Barrier Reef's Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty is one-time transferable to a subsequent purchaser. Keep your warranty paperwork and serial number, and read the full written warranty for its conditions.

Q: How do I keep my pool warranty valid?
A: Keep your water balanced, don't drain the pool without calling first, and keep your paperwork. Finish warranties assume water chemistry stays in range. Barrier Reef's warranty covers the pool shell only, so the written document governs. See who covers what.

Rates and terms depend on the lender and your credit, so talk to iTop about your options when we go through your price. Our financing guide compares all four in plain English.

Q: What is the monthly payment on a pool?

## Guides

### Rectangle, freeform or kidney? Picking a shape
The best pool shape depends on how you'll use the water and what your house looks like. Rectangles give the most swimming length and suit modern homes, freeforms feel like a resort, and kidney and plunge shapes fit smaller yards. iTop Pools in Jacksonville can model any Barrier Reef shape in 3D. Key takeaways Rectangles give the most usable swimming length and suit modern homes. Freeform curves feel like a resort and blend with natural stone and palms. Kidney and plunge shapes suit lanai corners and townhome lots. Shape is mostly about how you'll use the water and what your house looks like. Who should choose a rectangular pool? Clean lines suit modern and transitional homes. They also give the most usable swimming length, so they're great for laps. Try the Aussie, Bondi or Whitsunday. Who should choose a freeform pool? Curves feel like a resort and blend with palms and natural stone. Try Coral Sea or Billabong Cove. Who should choose a kidney or plunge pool? Soft, classic and compact. Kidney shapes wrap nicely around a lanai corner, and plunge pools fit townhome lots. Try Opal or Milano. Not sure? Take the 30-second pool finder on our homepage, or drop any model into the 3D studio and walk around it.

### Permits, HOAs and Florida pool safety rules
Every inground pool in Northeast Florida needs a building permit, and most neighborhoods also need HOA approval. Florida law also requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature. iTop Pools in Jacksonville prepares the drawings and handles the county and HOA submittals for you. Key takeaways Every inground pool in Northeast Florida needs a building permit. Most neighborhoods also need HOA approval, and iTop handles both. Florida law requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature. Every inground pool in Northeast Florida needs a building permit, and most neighborhoods also need HOA approval. iTop handles both. Do I need a building permit? Your city or county reviews the site plan, setbacks, electrical and drainage before work starts, then inspects during the build. Will my HOA need to approve it? Many communities, including Nocatee, Julington Creek and Ponte Vedra neighborhoods, want drawings, materials and sometimes colors before approving. Our 3D design and site plan make this faster. What does Florida's pool safety law require? Florida's Residential Swimming Pool Safety Act (Chapter 515, Florida Statutes) requires a new residential pool to have at least one approved safety feature. Options include a compliant barrier or fence, an approved safety cover, exit alarms on doors and windows that open to the pool, or self-closing, self-latching doors. We'll recommend the safety option that fits your family and your county's inspection, and build it into your quote. Requirements vary by jurisdiction. Your permit reviewer has the final word.

### How to choose a finish color
Choose a pool finish by the water color you want, not the color of the sample. Light finishes such as Arctic give turquoise water, while dark finishes such as Ocean look deeper and more reflective. Depth, shade and your deck all change the result, so see real samples on your site visit. Key takeaways Barrier Reef's US range has seven finishes. Light finishes give turquoise water, and dark finishes look deeper and more reflective. Depth, shade and deck color all change how the water looks. Barrier Reef's US range has seven finishes: Aquamarine, Arctic, California, Evening Sky, Ocean, Sandstone and Silver Mist. Should I choose a light or dark finish? Light finishes such as Arctic and Sandstone give turquoise, Caribbean-style water. Dark finishes such as Ocean and Evening Sky look deeper and more reflective, like a lake. What changes the color of the water? Depth. The deep end always reads darker than the steps. Sky and shade. A screen enclosure softens and darkens the water slightly. Deck. Light travertine makes water look brighter. Charcoal pavers make it look moodier. Compare any two finishes side by side in our color lab, then ask us to bring real samples to your site visit.

The upgrades owners use most are a tanning ledge, a spa and a heat pump, which stretches the swim season in Florida's mild winters. LED lighting and automation are cheap to add during the build and awkward to add later. iTop Pools can price each one so you can decide. Key takeaways A tanning ledge is one of the upgrades owners use most. Heat pumps suit Florida's mild winters and stretch the swim season. Lighting and automation are cheap during the build and awkward to add later. Some upgrades get used every day. Others get forgotten. Here's what we see owners use most. Is a tanning ledge worth it? A shallow shelf, usually under a foot of water. It's where chairs, toddlers and morning coffee end up. Highly recommended. Should I add a spa? Choose a shell with an integrated spa, like Sydney Harbour, or add a raised spillover spa. Great for cooler months. Do I need a heat pump? Florida's mild winters suit heat pumps well, and they stretch your swim season. Are LED lighting and automation worth it? Color LEDs and phone control for pump, lights and heat. ### Hurricane prep for your pool
Before a hurricane, leave your fiberglass pool full, because high groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell upward. Turn off equipment power and secure loose items. Don't restart equipment until it's dry and debris is cleared, and call iTop Pools if anything looks off after the storm. Key takeaways Never drain a fiberglass pool, because high groundwater can push an empty shell up. Don't restart equipment until it's dry and debris is cleared. Call iTop after the storm if anything looks off. Northeast Florida storms are part of life. Here's how to prepare your pool. Do Keep the pool full. The water's weight helps hold the shell in place. Turn off pump, heater and lights at the breaker. Bring in furniture, toys and loose décor. Raise chlorine slightly before the storm. Don't Never drain a fiberglass pool. High groundwater after heavy rain can push an empty shell up. Don't restart equipment until it's dry and debris is cleared. After the storm, call us if anything looks off. We'd rather check than have you guess.

### Fiberglass pool pros and cons
The main advantages of a fiberglass pool are fast installation, a smooth low-maintenance surface and no resurfacing or liner replacement. The main drawbacks are a limited choice of molded shapes and sizes, and shipping limits on width. It suits most families, though not anyone who needs a fully custom design. Key takeaways Barrier Reef puts a typical install at 2–6 weeks once permits clear. The smooth gelcoat gives algae less to grip. You choose from molded designs, so fully custom shapes need concrete. What are the advantages of a fiberglass pool? Speed. The shell is made in a factory and set in one piece, so there's much less on-site construction. Lower upkeep. The non-porous gelcoat gives algae less to grip, and Barrier Reef estimates vinyl pools use about 50% more chemicals. Fewer big bills. There's no plaster to resurface and no liner to replace. Comfort. The surface is smooth underfoot. Warranty. Barrier Reef offers a Lifetime Limited Structural Warranty, transferable once, and a 15-year finish warranty against blistering. What are the disadvantages of a fiberglass pool? Set shapes. You choose from molds, so there's no vanishing edge or one-off layout. Size limits. Shells travel by road, which limits width. Barrier Reef's models here top out at 16' wide. Access. The shell needs a route into your yard, and sometimes a crane. Don't drain it yourself. Groundwater can push an empty shell upward, so draining always needs professional advice. Who should choose something else? If your yard needs a truly custom shape, concrete is the better answer. If the lowest upfront price matters most, compare vinyl. See fiberglass vs concrete vs vinyl for the full comparison, or what a pool costs in Jacksonville. Sources: Barrier Reef Pools USA (install time, chemical use, warranty).

### What size pool is best for a Florida backyard?
The best pool size is the one that leaves room for your deck and meets your setbacks. Most families look at 27–35 foot shells, while lots under about 30 feet of usable length suit compact and plunge models. iTop Pools in Jacksonville measures your yard on a free site visit and tells you which shells fit. Key takeaways Measure what's left after setbacks, easements and the deck, not the whole yard. Barrier Reef models here run from 16'6" to 40' long. Length matters for swimmers, and width matters for play. How much room do you need around a pool? Start with your usable area, after setbacks and easements on your survey, and allow for a walkable deck on every side. As a first estimate, add about 8 feet to the shell's length and width for a 4-foot walkway. Your county and HOA rules decide the real limits, so confirm them before you fall in love with a size. How big should a pool be for your family? Laps. Long, straight rectangles such as the Bondi give the most swimming length. Family play. Width matters more than length. The Aussie is 15'9" wide in both sizes. Lounging. Look for a lounge area, as on the Outback Lounger. Cooling off. A plunge pool may be all you need. Does a bigger pool cost much more to run? Bigger pools hold more water to treat and heat. Barrier Reef's models here range from about 3,100 gallons for the Crispin to about 28,350 gallons for the Whitsunday 40 Deep, so the difference is significant. ### Saltwater vs chlorine pools
A saltwater pool is still a chlorine pool: a salt cell makes chlorine from salt in the water, so you buy and handle less chlorine and many people find the water feels softer. You still need to test and balance it. iTop Pools in Jacksonville can include a salt system in your fiberglass pool. Key takeaways Salt systems still produce chlorine, so you test the same way. Salt cells are an added piece of equipment that eventually needs replacing. Ask about salt compatibility with your deck and nearby materials. How does a saltwater pool work? You add salt to the water, and a cell in the equipment turns it into chlorine as the water passes through. The pool is sanitized by chlorine either way. The difference is how the chlorine gets there. What are the pros and cons of a salt system? Pro: You handle less chlorine day to day. Pro: Many owners find the water feels softer. Con: It adds equipment to the upfront cost, and the cell eventually needs replacing. Con: Salt can affect some natural stone and metal, so ask us about your deck and fittings. Which is better for a fiberglass pool? Either can work. Follow the water chemistry ranges on your handover sheet, because Barrier Reef's finish warranty assumes balanced water. See your first 30 days as a pool owner for typical targets. Add a salt system in the estimator to see how it changes your budget.

### Screen enclosures for Florida pools
A screen enclosure is an aluminum frame with screen that keeps out leaves and insects, and it's common across Northeast Florida. It adds a significant line item, with size, height and roof style driving the cost. It also slightly softens water color. iTop Pools in Jacksonville can design and price one with your pool. Key takeaways An enclosure keeps out leaves and insects, which cuts cleaning. Size, height and roof style drive the cost. Screen softens and slightly darkens the look of the water. Is a screen enclosure worth it in Florida? Many Northeast Florida owners think so. An enclosure keeps insects away in the evening and keeps leaves out of the water, so there's less skimming. On the other hand, it adds cost and changes the view from your house, so try it both ways in the 3D studio. What affects the cost of a pool enclosure? Footprint. The area you enclose, including the deck. Height and roof style. Taller and more complex roofs use more material. Your home. How it connects to the house and lanai. iTop gives you one written price for the pool, deck and enclosure after the site visit. See fiberglass pool cost in Jacksonville. Does an enclosure change the color of the water? Slightly. Screen softens and darkens the water a little. See how to choose a finish color. What about hurricanes? Plan for storm season, and read our hurricane prep guide. Your permit reviewer has the final word on what's required for your site.

### Fiberglass pools and high water tables
Fiberglass pools can work well in areas with high water tables, such as parts of Northeast Florida, when they're installed for the site. The key rule is never to drain the pool without professional advice, because groundwater can push an empty shell upward. iTop Pools in Jacksonville checks site conditions on the free visit. Key takeaways Groundwater pushes up on a pool, and water inside the pool holds it down. Never drain a fiberglass pool without professional advice. Heavy rain can raise groundwater, so take extra care after storms. Why does a high water table matter for a pool? A pool is a shell sitting in the ground. Water in the surrounding soil pushes up on it, and the water inside holds it down. When a pool is full, that's rarely a concern. When it's empty and the ground is wet, the shell can move. Can you install a fiberglass pool where the water table is high? Yes, with planning. Your installer should assess site conditions before digging and deal with groundwater during excavation and backfill. We backfill evenly while the pool fills with water, to keep pressure balanced. See your build, week by week. What should you never do? Never drain a fiberglass pool yourself. Always call us first, especially after heavy rain or a storm. Does it affect the warranty? Barrier Reef's warranty has its own conditions, so keep your paperwork and read the full document. See who covers what.
